description: tt marks a written T by its first original word, head(after($m)), as tail-terms of the CLL grammar marks a written vau. That word can belong to what follows tt: here it is the T that ends the text. So the second condition of the mark, text($) ≠ text($m), keeps tt from marking an empty optional. With the guard, c fails, a is the one parse that the ranking keeps, and the check passes. Without it, tt is marked with its [T #] empty, c elides T at the place where a does, and the two tie. The guard decides the main parse, so the check does not change this result (engine §7.5, grammars/syntax/cll.md).
grammar:
%ambiguity-resolution late-elision elision-only
%rule text a | b | c
%rule a A m [+T] T
%rule b A m [+T] [+T] T
%rule c A $t(tt) T
%conditions ~written ⊆ tags($t)
%rule # [{F}]
%rule m B
%rule tt $m(m) [+T #] <text($) ≠ text($m) ∧ T ⊆ tags(head(after($m))) ⟹ ~written>
